question: pr3389
answer:
The diff is a redirect-header refactor. It moves `same_origin`, `is_https_redirect`, and `port_or_default` from `httpx/_utils.py` into `httpx/_client.py`, adds leading underscores, and preserves their logic. Five existing tests move from `tests/test_utils.py` to `tests/client/test_headers.py` without assertion changes.

**Affected callers and behavior.** `BaseClient._redirect_headers` is the sole production caller. Both `Client` and `AsyncClient` reach it through `_build_redirect_request`, including when they populate `response.next_request`. Same-origin redirects preserve `Host` and `Authorization`. Cross-origin redirects rewrite `Host` and strip `Authorization`, with an exception for same-host HTTP port 80 to HTTPS port 443 upgrades. The existing end-to-end auth coverage is in `tests/client/test_redirects.py`. [httpx/_client.py](<work>/pr3389-rules-official-codex/httpx/_client.py:545)

**Risks.** I found no runtime regression in the diff. Downstream code importing the removed helpers from `httpx._utils`, or importing the two previously exposed names from `httpx._client`, will break. The only in-repo importer was `httpx/_client.py`, which this diff updates. The relocated `test_same_origin` and `test_not_same_origin` have a pre-existing blind spot because both URLs normalize to the same authority in each test, so the `Host` assertions can pass even if the origin check takes the wrong branch.
